instruction: Learn from actual reference promo content, never from filenames alone. Compare a new promo against references from the same show first, then use general references only when show-specific examples are unavailable.

Hook.P0 Topper: Show-specific dialogue or impossible situation in 13 words or fewer; opens an unanswered emotional or high-stakes question.
Hook.P0 Above Avg: Strong specific hook with minor loss of immediacy or curiosity.
Hook.P1 Avg: Understandable hook but familiar, longer, or less show-specific.
Hook.P2 Rejected: Generic, confusing, low-stakes, or gives away the payoff.

Context & World Clarity.P0 Topper: Quickly identifies lead, setting, relationship, threat and stakes using only source truth; creates intrigue rather than summary.
Context & World Clarity.P0 Above Avg: Clear context with small gaps in world or character motivation.
Context & World Clarity.P1 Avg: Basic situation is understandable but emotional or world context is thin.
Context & World Clarity.P2 Rejected: Listener cannot tell who is involved, what is happening, or why it matters.

Sequence & Plot Movement.P0 Topper: Every beat changes the question or stakes; chronology/flashback/jumble is clear and purposeful.
Sequence & Plot Movement.P0 Above Avg: Plot moves well with one slower or less essential beat.
Sequence & Plot Movement.P1 Avg: Some movement but connective logic or escalation is uneven.
Sequence & Plot Movement.P2 Rejected: Passive summary, random jumps, or no meaningful consequence.

Scene Design.P0 Topper: Each scene has tension/curiosity, character reveal, and meaningful story movement; dialogue is cinematic and attributed.
Scene Design.P0 Above Avg: Strong scenes with occasional reporting or generic dialogue.
Scene Design.P1 Avg: Scenes work individually but lack one of setup, reveal, or movement.
Scene Design.P2 Rejected: Scenes are mostly exposition, interchangeable, or disconnected from source.

Pacing & Transitions.P0 Topper: Emotion breathes early, then the final third accelerates through earned bridges and sharper lines.
Pacing & Transitions.P0 Above Avg: Good rhythm with minor drag or abrupt cut.
Pacing & Transitions.P1 Avg: Uneven rhythm; escalation or transitions need tightening.
Pacing & Transitions.P2 Rejected: Flat, rushed, repetitive, or confusing after cuts.

Ending, Callback & CTA.P0 Topper: Episode 1 callback feels earned; final conflict remains unresolved; 3–4 specific urgent questions and Pocket FM CTA.
Ending, Callback & CTA.P0 Above Avg: Effective cliffhanger and CTA with one missed or weaker element.
Ending, Callback & CTA.P1 Avg: Some curiosity remains but callback, escalation, or CTA specificity is limited.
Ending, Callback & CTA.P2 Rejected: Full resolution, generic questions, missing callback/CTA, or no listening reason.

Follow successful promos pattern.P0 Topper: Matches the same show's winning architecture, emotional promise, escalation density, character treatment and CTA rhythm while remaining original.
Follow successful promos pattern.P0 Above Avg: Clearly shares winning-show traits with a few weaker choices.
Follow successful promos pattern.P1 Avg: Uses some useful traits but feels generic or inconsistent with the show's winners.
Follow successful promos pattern.P2 Rejected: Resembles rejected patterns: exposition-heavy, generic, source-disconnected, or low-curiosity.

Mental Impact & Recall Value.P0 Topper: Lead, conflict, emotional promise and next-listen question remain vivid after the promo.
Mental Impact & Recall Value.P0 Above Avg: Memorable central conflict with one blurred emotional or character beat.
Mental Impact & Recall Value.P1 Avg: Some memorable moments but the promise or characters fade.
Mental Impact & Recall Value.P2 Rejected: Forgettable, emotionally flat, confusing, or unlike the show.

independent_scoring_protocol.ruleScores: Score only against the authoritative Rule set learning document and source-grounded execution requirements. Do not use topper, average, rejected, pattern signature, benchmark style, or pattern-learning observations to raise or lower this column.
independent_scoring_protocol.patternScores: Score only against observed successful/average/below-average promo architecture, labelled examples and source-grounded show patterns. Do not use the Rule set thresholds or mechanical rule compliance to raise or lower this column.
independent_scoring_protocol.truth_guard: Before scoring either column, verify every character, event, relationship, power, object and outcome against the selected show's source. Put unsupported claims in contradictions, lower fidelity, and never treat an invented detail as evidence. Keep source truth separate from creative pattern fit.
independent_scoring_protocol.different_scores: The two columns are independent measurements and may legitimately differ. Never copy a score, final score, tier, strength or deduction from one column into the other.

deep_cross_show_learning.purpose: Use these observations as architecture-level pattern signals after reading the selected show's source and same-show references. They are not hard rules and must not override source truth.
shared_winner_architecture: Start with a character-specific contradiction, not a world glossary: weak person with dangerous identity, rejected spouse with hidden competence, ordinary boy holding forbidden power, or apparently powerless person making an impossible choice.
Convert the premise into a chain of performed events: pressure -> choice -> visible consequence -> reaction from a higher-status or dangerous character -> new identity/threat question.

Delay the largest supernatural/status reveal until the audience has emotionally invested in the lead's wound, desire, relationship or sacrifice; the reveal should change the meaning of the earlier conflict.

Use one dominant emotional spine and one supporting mystery. Promos lose pattern fit when they run several equal storylines, list many characters, or switch from romance to mythology to comedy without a bridge.
End at the first irreversible reversal or interruption, before resolution. A cliffhanger is strongest when the final image is concrete and the questions grow directly from it.
Length is neutral. Reward new pressure, reveal, decision or consequence per beat; penalize repeated labels, recap, production directions and scenes that only add names or powers.
negative_signals_that_should_lower_multi: A dramatic opening that is not paid off later should lower Hook, Sequence, Ending and Mental Impact rather than receiving hook credit alone.
A power, object or villain introduced only in narration without a character choice or visible consequence should lower Scene Design, Sequence and Follow successful promos pattern.
A promo beginning after the main event, or functioning as an extension without enough standalone context, should lower Context, Sequence, Ending and Pattern Fit.
Repeated humiliation, poverty, weakness, betrayal or family labels without a changed consequence should lower Sequence, Pacing, Scene Design and Recall Value.
A broad final list of mysteries after the strongest scene should lower Ending even when the promo contains a CTA; questions must be specific, limited and attached to the final image.
A source mismatch is not a creative pattern difference. Unsupported powers, relationships, identities or outcomes must be treated as contradictions and cannot earn pattern credit.

parameter_deep_signals.Hook: Measure the first meaningful beat, not the title or character list. Ask whether the first line creates a contradiction with a person, desire and consequence, and whether the hook remains open after the first scene. Reward specificity, compression and show DNA; deduct for generic fantasy claims, backstory before conflict, mid-story openings and unpaid spectacle.
parameter_deep_signals.Context & World Clarity: Measure selective clarity, not the amount of information. The listener should understand the lead's present position, the key relationship, the immediate threat and the source-specific promise before the first major transition. Reward context embedded in conflict; deduct for biographies, mythology dumps, too many names and unexplained chronology.
parameter_deep_signals.Sequence & Plot Movement: Map each beat as an event with an actor, choice and consequence. A new beat counts only when it changes danger, status, knowledge, relationship or goal. Reward emotional-to-supernatural causality and purposeful flashbacks; deduct when scenes are interchangeable, resolved before the next beat, or stitched as episode summaries.
parameter_deep_signals.Scene Design: For each major scene, identify pressure, action, reaction and consequence. Reward attributed dialogue that forces a decision and visual proof of change. Deduct for narration describing what could be played, SFX/production notes standing in for drama, repeated insults and spectacle disconnected from the lead's choice.
parameter_deep_signals.Pacing & Transitions: Judge pressure density and bridge quality rather than word count. Strong promos breathe around the wound or relationship, compress repeated history, then accelerate toward a concrete reversal. Deduct for repetition, long static dialogue, unexplained time jumps, location churn and tonal shifts without a causal or emotional bridge.
parameter_deep_signals.Ending, Callback & CTA: The ending should be the next unavoidable question created by the final consequence. Reward an earned callback, an unresolved irreversible event, one dominant final image and three or four concrete questions followed by CTA. Deduct for resolution, vague questions, a CTA detached from the story or a cliffhanger that merely repeats an earlier reveal.
parameter_deep_signals.Narration/Dialogue Balance: Score function, not percentage. Narration should orient, bridge and intensify imagery; dialogue should expose character, create pressure or deliver a reveal. Deduct when characters explain their own biographies, when narrator praise replaces proof, or when every line has the same emotional temperature.
parameter_deep_signals.Mental Impact & Recall Value: Test the one-sentence memory after the promo: can the listener name the lead, wound, emotional promise and final question, plus one concrete image? Reward contrast and status reversal. Deduct when names, powers and subplots compete for memory or when the final image is generic.
parameter_deep_signals.Follow successful promos pattern: Compare architecture and emotional promise against same-show toppers, not isolated props. A new promo can use a different entry hook and still fit if it preserves the show's pressure engine, character role, escalation logic, reveal timing and ending rhythm. Penalize surface imitation, copied finale images, generic genre language and missing show-specific relationship logic.

evidence_handling.same_show_priority: Use selected-show topper, average and rejected references first. General cross-show signals are tie-breakers only.
evidence_handling.source_priority: Use the show source to verify every character, relationship, object, power, event and outcome before awarding pattern credit.
evidence_handling.anchor_priority: Named training anchors calibrate the overall pattern score only when content matches; they do not automatically set every parameter or justify copying a score.
evidence_handling.uncertainty: When the evidence is incomplete, lower confidence and explain the missing pattern evidence instead of inventing a match.
